summary: 1911 lookout cab on a 50-ft observation tower on Mount Greylock; discontinued after 1913 for poor visibility; cab removed; summit reachable by road.

facts.design: 50-foot observation tower (register says iron; the Willhite history page says steel) with a lookout cab built on top in 1911
facts.status_note: Lookout cab removed after 1913 and the steel tower left standing; no source says whether that tower still stands

access.note: Summit reachable by road today per the Willhite history page; the old lookout site is not described separately

facts.agency: State Forester, Berkshire County office (per the Willhite history page)

events.note: Lookout cab built on top of a pre-existing 50-foot steel observation tower
Operations started October 17, 1911; Thomas Buxton had been the fire lookout that season
Use discontinued at the end of the 1913 fire season due to poor visibility
Date registered September 3, 2008; nominated by Henry Isenberg

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS gives 3,491 ft (1,064 m); the Willhite page gives 3,487 feet. The record's 1064.1 m matches FFLOS, so FFLOS is kept.
FFLOS calls the tower iron; the Willhite page calls it steel. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Two sources. The 1911 to 1913 detail, the Thomas Buxton staffing and the deputy-warden meeting rest on the Willhite page, an independent history site; no state record (Massachusetts DCR or Mount Greylock Reservation) was read. Elevation conflict: 3,491 ft (FFLOS) versus 3,487 ft (Willhite); record kept at 1064.1 m. The brief's status 'gone' is kept: the cab is gone, but the steel tower's fate is unknown. The Veterans War Memorial Tower is described only in the Willhite page; its build date is unverified and it is not confirmed to stand on the 1911 site. No photos collected.
